_README: Declared canonical quantities (spec SS5 G5). Hand-written against the corpus, NOT inferred.
Every `canonical` and `alsoTaught` entry carries a quote that must appear verbatim at its
cited location - check-quantities.mjs verifies that, so this table cannot drift away from
her material without failing the build.
canonical   : the value the pack must use. Her material, her number.
alsoTaught  : a DIFFERENT value that ALSO appears in her material. Recorded, not resolved -
where she contradicts herself the pack says so rather than silently picking.
rejected    : values that are simply WRONG for this concept. Hard build failure.
needsHers   : values that are not wrong (a textbook figure, a rounding) but must not appear
WITHOUT her value alongside them in the same card. Fails only if hers is absent.
notTaught   : the concept appears nowhere in her material at any value.
match       : REQUIRED wherever rejected/needsHers is used. An explicit context regex that
must be present in the card for the rule to apply. Declared by hand, never
inferred - an earlier inferring version of this check tagged nitrogen's 592.8
as an oxygen value and flagged a correct range as a contradiction.
requireRange: {unit, pattern} - only fires when the card uses that unit, and is satisfied by
any phrasing the declared pattern accepts ("0.5-1", "0.5 to 1"). Declared, so
the check cannot fail a correct card for writing the range a different way.
`range: true` means the canonical IS the interval; citing one endpoint alone is wrong.

atmospheric-po2.concept: Partial pressure of O₂ in atmospheric air at sea level

alsoTaught.note: implied by her own worked formula on the next slide (20.8% of 760), which disagrees with her table's 159.6 (21%). Both are hers.

needsHers.why: textbook rounding of her 159.6. Not wrong, but the pack must not state it without her figure - card #53 cites 159.6 while #57/#59/#62/#64 say 159.

rejected.why: a different textbook's figure (0.04% of 760). Her slide gives 0.2, consistent with the 0.03% in her own formula. README claims this was corrected; it survives in card #65 and glossary #43.

anatomical-dead-space.why: Zero hits for "dead space" anywhere in the 12,063-unit corpus. The pack asserts ~150 mL on five cards. Standard textbook value, but she teaches no figure, so it cannot be `taught` tier.
